Radar cross section (RCS) is defined as 4π times the ratio of scattered power density to incident power density from a target.
Shaping and radar absorbing materials (RAM) are the primary traditional techniques for RCS reduction.
Shaping reduces RCS by redirecting radar reflections away from the radar receiver.
RAM absorbs incident radar energy and converts it into heat, reducing reflected energy.
Most RAM coatings are narrowband and require precise application and thickness control.
Active cancellation involves emitting a signal from the target to destructively interfere with radar echoes.
Metamaterials are engineered composites with electromagnetic properties not found in natural materials.
Negative Index Metamaterials (NIM) have negative permittivity and permeability, resulting in negative refractive index.
Electromagnetic Bandgap (EBG) metamaterials control light propagation by prohibiting certain frequency bands.
Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) act as spatial filters, reflecting or transmitting specific frequencies.
Microstrip antennas have high RCS due to their ground plane and are common in military applications.
Metamaterials can enhance antenna performance by miniaturization, bandwidth expansion, gain enhancement, and RCS reduction.
The proposed metamaterial unit cell for RCS reduction includes a square loop and intersecting strips on the antenna ground plane.
Radar detection range depends on the fourth root of the RCS, so reducing RCS by 16 times halves detection range.
Active cancellation is more suitable for low-frequency RCSR due to broader scattering lobes at these frequencies.
Passive cancellation uses impedance loading to create destructive interference over narrow frequency bands.
RAMs are more effective at controlling backscattering than forward scattering.
Modern radars operate over a wide frequency range, necessitating broadband RCSR techniques.
Metamaterials enable control over electromagnetic wave propagation through their structure rather than composition.
The paper reviews recent research on metamaterial-based RCSR and proposes a new unit cell design.
